title: Engram
review: We present 2 new tracks from Mexico Citys Eisenheim each with their own deep house and cinematic qualities. Once Upon a Time takes melodic patterned synths, pianos, and tight percussion and fuses them all into one package while Nothing Rests; Everything Moves harkens back to the days of acid techno, breaks, and retro sounds.

title: Out of BK
review: Label head Eric Shans and long time producer Gatto team up to deliver a new EP called Out of BK. Deep, melodic, house cuts each offering up different sounds and textures meant for the dance floor and the after hours sessions. Theyve also remixed their own versions of the tracks injecting their own personal styles into them. Gatto infuses some deep tech into Out of BK and Eric some dub into Driving Into the Sun. Get in and take a trip.

tracks.title: Driving Into the Sun (Eric Shans Remix)

title: Idle
review: Stego is back on 3Bridge with 2 big house tunes that will shake your dance floors. From the chuggy grooves and deep chords of Idle to the melodic edginess of Git, these would make a great addition to your late night sets.
https://www.beatport.com/release/idle/4824129

title: Mediator
review: A new signing for the label, Yes Kovatz (aka Nicholas Ljeskovac) with 2 dub heavy melodic tunes. “Mediator” is a high energy techno influenced workout with a big delivery, while “Temporal Drifts” slows the pace down and cruises along with big pads, tight percussion, and lush chords.

title: Disco Wakeup
review: A new 2 tracker from Brooklyn, NY based producer, The Company Soundsystem with Cavalier. Deep house tunes with disco influences that bring the funk. Perfect for the spring and summer seasons and those sparkling nights on the dance floor.

title: Let Sleeping Dogs
review: A new signing for 3Bridge in 2024, UK producer Stego (Lee Martin) gives us 2 dance floor ready, melodic house tunes. Replete with big grooves, moving synth lines, and slick percussion – you’d do well to pick these up.

title: The Main Line
review: This new 3 tracker from label boss Eric Shans is the first music on 3Bridge Records for 2024. The title track is a groovy, techy workout meant for the later hours with big bright synths and nasty bass lines. “Voltage Divider” is a melodic house number with big drums, lush pads, and beautiful melodies, and “Nebula Pulse” is an exploration into dub house sounds with ethereal atmospheres and energetic rhythms.

title: Inside
review: For our last release of 2023, we have Gatto’s “Inside” a 2 tracker highlighting the melodic side of his production style. “Celebrate You” is replete with acid stabs, crystalline synth sounds, and great percussion. “Inside” is an ode to progressive breakbeat with cool vocal samples, thick basslines, and deep house chords. Releases December 1st, 2023 on Beatport and Spotify then 2 weeks later to the rest of the world.

title: Tribal Tattoo
review: Birmingham (UK) born, Steve ‘Griffo’ Griffiths returns in his Second City Firsts guise six years after his remix of KP Deep Mesh’s ‘Hemp’ here on the label. Steve’s latest track ‘Tribal Tattoo’ is a tribal house outing inspired by his love of the late ’80s/early ’90s Warriors Dance label that released such seminal tracks as ‘Koro Koro’ by No Smoke. ‘Tribal Tattoo’ is a full-on tribal groover with jazzy vibes and a huge drum breakdown. On remix duties, well known Nordic house music stalwart, Norway’s Ulf Moen Denneche aka Boblebad, known for his releases on labels such as Beatservice has created a more laid back, dreamy mix with his ‘Bubble Dub’.

title: Liquid Laser
review: 3Bridge Records welcomes Cologne based artist IPI (aka Christian Iparraguirre) with his new EP “Liquid Laser”. It’s 3 tracks of deep, funky, and melodic tech and it’s reminiscent of some of the sounds on the great label Kompakt, based in Cologne as well. The title track hits you with an urgent synth riff that glides over a thick bass line and tripped out vocal snippets. There’s a house music influence here blended well with the alternating claps, sharp hi-hats, and big beats. “Cristal Lake” offers up some lush dub chords, filtering leads, and subtle melody, and the closer “Breezey” is like a steady sunset car ride on a highway. It’s cloaked in big pads and washes with a beautiful piano melody highlighting its beauty.

title: Words Unspoken
review: The duo Lenz returns to 3Bridge Records for a lovely spring time melodic tune called”Words Unspoken”. Moon Aton’s spoken word over deep, lush pads, big grooves, and pristine synth sounds make this is a great addition to your melodic arsenal of musical weapons

title: Around the Sphere
review: Long time producers Eric Shans and Gatto team up for the 1st release of 2023 for the label called “Around the Sphere’. The title is fitting as this EP touches upon multiple styles of electronic music. Big house grooves techno influences, and chilled out workouts; they’re all here replete with memorable melodies and atmospheres.

“Electric Surge” kicks things off with tribal drums, crystalline arpeggios, and smacking percussion gluing the rhythms going over the course of the track. This is meant for the late nights and those dark smoky rooms. “Around The Sphere” ups the techno energy a bit with an analog bass line that filters throughout, along with big acid squelches, pristine percussion, and soft ethereal pads serving as a juxtaposition to the tough sounding beats. “Liquid Comedown” takes futuristic riffs, big synth lines, and dramatic strings giving this one some moodiness and mystery and “Numbers” gives us lush grooves, meticulously programmed drums, and soothing sounds rounding off this great EP.

title: Change
review: Renowned New York DJs and producers Sleepy and Boo are back on 3Bridge Records for the label’s final release of the year, making their return to the imprint with the stunning four-track EP Change. With this release, Sleepy and Boo have delivered four standout creations for the dance floor and beyond. The title track “Change” sets the pace with a pulsating bassline, synth lines that drift in and out, a moody, hypnotic chord progression, and energetic percussion, all fusing together to uplift the collective spirit. “Transition” continues into late-night territory with urgent, dub-flavored chord stabs, cool vocal hits, and an upfront melodic lead; this track is all about the groove. The third cut “Adjust” brings in the morning vibes with euphoric chords, shuffling percussion, and a sturdy analog bass line to hold everything together. Crossing the lines between deep house and techier sounds, this one closes with a memorable synth solo that will linger long after the night is over. To wrap things up on this stellar EP, Sleepy and Boo’s “Resolve” offers up soothing pads, soaring strings and a gorgeous piano theme that radiates emotion, thoughtfulness and positivity. These four tracks have all been played to joyful dance floors, and together, showcase Sleepy and Boo’s diversity as producers, and ability to connect with the listener.

title: Kanterbury
review: Spanish producer Tony Crawm strikes back in 2022 on 3Bridge with this huge two tracker, “Kanterbury”. These are meant for the dark, foggy rooms in the peak time hours where everyone is ready to get down and dirty.

The title track takes a moving arpeggiated bass, quirky vocal snippets, punchy snare rolls, and a mega tight groove which will have a floor moving. “This This” goes more the sweaty techno-route with racing hi-hats, swirling atmospheres, and fat bottom end.
“Kanterbury” will surely light up your DJ sets ; you can almost hear the strobe lights emanating from tracks.

title: Cloud Bursts
review: One of the main 3Bridge Records bosses Eric Shans is back with his first original music of 2022, “Cloud Bursts”. Always trying to push the envelope both creatively and sonically, it’s a killer 2 tracker that will fill your dance floors with energy and good vibes.

The title track takes a monstrous bass line, thumping drums, anthemic chords, and twinkling arpeggios which really go for the late night peak time sound. “Fractals” focuses on thick analog sounding low end, big synths, melodic pads, and clean retro-future percussion, as well as some fun vocals thrown in the mix.
You’d do well to pick this single up for your digital crates.

title: Chunky
review: Gatto is back on 3Bridge with his first release of 2022 with his newest single “Chunky”. This two track EP of deep and melodic funky house is truly a groovy affair.

The title track showcases subwoofer type low-end, big waves of melodic pads, unique percussion patterns, and subtle vocal chops and “What It Is” takes a bit more of a tech-house approach with a rumbling bass, smacking snares, and analog stabs. It’s a perfect B-side highlighting the contrasts of the lights and the darks on the aural canvas.

title: Muntjac
review: A new signing for 3Bridge Records, the British duo Dadhaus with their new single “Muntjac”. It’s a great way to start off 2022 and it features a remix by the Nottingham based producer Tim Tonal.

The original mix is comprised of big analog stabs, shuffling old school drum machine beats, and ’80s type synth pads which give the track a retro-modern feel. Tim Tonal’s remix goes straight for the dance floor in the peak hours with a repeated funky vocal line, buttery percussion, and catchy arpeggios.
We’re very psyched to have this one see the light of day on the label.

title: Gettin’ It
review: We welcome New England based producer Pete Ahern to 3Bridge Records for our last release of 2021 with his EP ‘Gettin’ It’. 2 tracks of super groovy deep house for your listening pleasure.

The title track takes slick vocal chops and spreads them out over fluttering, galloping percussion, old school synth lines and steady syncopated rhythms. This one will definitely pack a dance floor. “Elsa” takes similar elements but wraps them in a more late night motif. A big piano riff glues the female vox line to the tough percussion, tech-laden riffs, and energetic beats.

title: Sad Eyes
artistLine: DJ Joma, Eric Shans, Moon Aton
review: We’re happy to have the talented Irish producer, DJ Joma and the great singer Moon Aton on 3Bridge Records with their single “Sad Eyes”. It’s a classic sounding, deep melodic progressive track with big sawtooth baselines, lush chords, and smooth percussion which would be perfect as an opener or a peak time driver. 3Bridge label head Eric Shans is on remixing duties adding his trademark signature throwback sounds with fat bottom end, swirling arpeggios, and an epic breakdown.

title: Follow the Signs
review: 3Bridge Records head honcho Eric Shans returns to the label release roster with his new EP ‘Follow the Signs’, a 3 tracker which runs the gamut of styles all while retaining the melodic, groovy tones he’s known for.

The title track is a great example of a classic yet updated deep house sound replete with 80s analog bass lines, smooth distant pads, and big drums. This will certainly keep a dance floor moving. ‘Space or Matter’ comes next and it takes a bit of a different direction with squelchy acid, energetic percussion, grand melodies, and fun spoken word samples. ‘At Last’ closes things out and takes Eric’s bittersweet, melancholy sound and ups the ante with beautifully structured chord progressions, expansive strings, soft low end, and ethereal yearning vocals.

title: Archetypes
review: Mexico City based artist Eisenheim is back on 3Bridge with a killer EP called “Archetypes”. It features 2 original tracks with remixes by Primordial Om and Anduaga.

Opening track “Archetype 1:Selbst” is a foray into melodic breakbeat oriented electronica with mystical ethereal voices, big arpeggios, and cinematic pads. “Archetype 2: Anima” ventures into lush deep house territory with big drums, groovy bass lines, and classical music influences. The remix from Anduaga brings these elements and wraps them in a peak time techno affair made for those late night big rooms, and Primordial Om’s version gives the track a breakbeat injection with shuffling loops, racing 16th patterns, warped melodies, and bottom heavy low end.
Here at the label trying we’re always trying to push new and inspiring sounds and this EP is no exception.

tracks.title: Archetype II: Anima (Primordial Om Arcane Tarot 22 Remix)

title: Miss You
review: Regular Gatto returns to 3Bridge for 2021 with the EP “Miss You” which is made of of two extremely deep tracks laced with melody and features a remix by label head Eric Shans.

The title track coasts along with ethereal synth backdrops, swirling melodies, and ambient washes. A perfect sunrise track for the upcoming warm months. Eric’s remix goes for the dance floor with big bold melodies, tight percussion, and groovy riffs; it’s sure to do a number when dropped in a set. “Soul 2 Soul” closes things out with simple yet effective chord progressions, shimmering pads, and heady harmonics.
All original tracks (excluding the Eric Shans Remix) mixed by Franklin Santiago.

title: Dulcie Caught a Cricket
review: The Colour & Pitch label head honcho Will Sumsuch arrives on 3bridge Records for his first release and we’re super excited about it. It’s a single with remixes by 3Bridge Records’ creative director Eric Shans and label regular, Gatto. Dulcie is Will’s spider friend and he thought it’d be appropriate to dedicate a song to her.

The original is a lovely foray into acid house. A precise drum pattern glues the track together with an exceptional 303 bass line that rips through the track. It’s echoed by dramatic strings, playful arpeggios, and an overall groovy palette. Eric’s remix takes those elements and adds some trademark cinematic touches while keeping the groove intact. There’s also an interesting vocal sample that describes a dialogue with a spider which is quite bizarre, yet captivating. And to close things out, Gatto’s ‘Spider’s on Acid Mix’ goes in a hypnotic tech direction with big percussion, fat low end, and walls of atmosphere.
Catch this great single and get your acid fix.
Mastered by Jeff Clarke. Gatto’s version mixed and mastered by Carlos Ruiz. Artwork by Eric Shans

tracks.title: Dulcie Caught a Cricket (Eric Shans Remix)
Dulcie Caught a Cricket (Gatto's Spider's On Acid Mix)

title: Kurripinha
review: Tony Crawm (aka Antonio Laguna) is back on the label this year with a great 2 tracker, this time a collaboration with Fede Gonzalez.

Title track ‘Kurripinha’ sets the stage right out of the gate with a peak time dance floor filler. Big bottom end, energetic drums, twisted synth lines, and dubbed out vocals are the main foundations here. It’s one for the late night for the big crowded smokey rooms, cavernous warehouses, and huge sound stacks. ‘Don’t Tell Me’ follows up with equally as much energy but amps up the funk level a bit with warped vocals, a groovy bass line, and pristine percussion. If you need 2 tracks that will get folks moving, look no further

title: Alright
review: Austrian based producer Simon Sampler, who has a good few releases on the label, comes back in 2021 with a new EP, simply called ‘Alright’.

Opening title track is a driving foray into energetic deep house with a techy influence. Racing percussion, old school organ riffs, and a repeated soulful vocal are the main drivers here. ‘This Sick’ comes next and adds a funky guitar riff over a repeated phrase with chunky beats. ‘Constellations’ falls into the groovy techno category with big leads over shuffling drums, and ‘Open Shot’ closes things out slowing down the tempo a tad but not without a nice energy to coast to the end of the record

title: Figure and Form
review: 3Bridge Records welcomes Begoña back in 2021 for the release of ‘Figure and Form’, her followup to 2019’s Kaleidoscope EP. Begoña is one half of New York’s Sleepy & Boo, the 3Bridge regulars who have been on a creative tear with a number of releases on international labels recently and forthcoming, including Transmit, Miles from Mars, Mavic, Techniche and more. This EP once again impresses as a showcase for her solo work, featuring four tracks of dubbed-out dance floor grooves, merging melodic overtones with hypnotic, techno-styled rhythms.

‘Figure’ gets the EP started on an energetic and uplifting note, propelled by its lush chord progressions, echoing percussive crashes, and building, ethereal leads. This track is a definite crowd-pleaser that is destined for some positive dance floor memories. ‘Form’ comes next, and this track delves into melodic, groovy house territory, with upfront percussion, earthy low-end, big claps, and cavernous atmospheres. The third track ‘Outline’ dips deep into a dub direction, with delayed leads weaving in and out of the mix. Filtered chord stabs pick up the energy towards the end, with everything cascading into a meaningful crescendo. Closing things out is ‘Aspect’, which applies a more abstract approach to its sound, focusing on sparse percussion and mesmerizing leads and arpeggios. The finale is a pensive and haunting piano solo that wraps up this excellent EP.

Begoña’s sound has evolved and expanded since she debuted on 3Bridge Elements with her downtempo and Balearic productions. This fall, she made her debut on Spain’s Sacudan Records with the well-received Explorations EP. We’re excited to present ‘Figure and Form’ as the latest step forward in her sound.

title: Burn
review: We welcome Brooklyn based producer and DJ, Brian Burnside to the label to start of 2021 with his stellar release, ‘Burn’. 3 slices of dance floor oriented music each flavored with different spices.

‘Relavator’ starts the EP off with a great energy burst. A chunky, thick bass line, punchy drums, and a soulful vocal are the guiding factors here as it straddles the line between the sounds of house and techno. ‘Labrea to Dekalb’ goes into full on deep house territory with soft Chicago-sounding pads, slick percussion, and melodic riffs that highlight the groove. ‘Quarantine’ closes things out and it’s the darkest of the 3 with a nasty bass line, twisted patterns, and great synth lines.
We’re psyched to start off a new year with some great music. You’d do well to add this release to your record boxes.

title: The Best Of 3Bridge : 2020
review: We’re happy to proudly present our annual best of the 3Bridge Records. 2020 has been a wild year on a lot of levels but there’s been no shortage of great music being made by awesome artists. So, enjoy and we’ll see you in 2021!

title: Cosmic Love
review: For the last original release on the label in 2020, we bring back the prolific producer, Gatto. His new EP ‘Cosmic Love’ is similar in nature to his previous EP ‘Sleeping Giants’ in that it highlights moody, analog textures with warm, uplifting melodies, and beats. It’s a perfect slice of harmony and calm against the backdrop of a chaotic year.

The title track gently coasts like a boat on an ocean wave in slow motion. Rich, painterly sounds highlight the piece along with deep bass and percussion with splashes of effects traveling in and out of the aural spectrum. Grandiose, yet subtle in its delivery, it’s a must hear. ‘Deep Science’ also echoes these same motifs, but the drums have a more live feel with acoustic hats, snares, and claps filling the spaces between. Big melodic synth pads drive the song home as if you were driving home with a cityscape in the distance after a great night with friends.
We’re happy to be closing our original music in 2020 with this EP.

title: Perception
review: New York’s Sleepy & Boo make their return to 3Bridge Records with their latest release ‘Perception’, a four-track exploration of deep, melodic and dub-inspired house vibes. Shining with positivity and hope, this set of tracks focuses on the promise of tomorrow into a collection of polished grooves that will have us all dancing as the seasons change.

Led by a haunting piano melody and insistent bass line, the title cut ‘Perception’ sets the stage perfectly for the rest of the EP. Loose percussion provides the foundation as this track builds to a euphoric crescendo of strings and keys, with a deep atmosphere that fuses a classic house sensibility with contemporary energy.

‘Expectation’ moves things forward persuasively with a sun-soaked aura that conjures up blissful memories of days past, aided by its prominent chord progression and generous doses of reverb and delay. This track perfectly demonstrates the EP’s ethos of uplifting, encouraging sounds.

Sleepy & Boo are no strangers to featuring dub influences in their tracks, and ‘Impressions’ continues that practice in an exceptional manner. This excursion modulates between stripped-down and exhilarating, with a firm fusion of memorable chords, synth riffs and energetic drums.

Wrapping things up is ‘Notion’, a wistful summation of the EPs’ themes that points the dance floor to brighter days ahead. This track is all about the six chord progression that anchors the groove, as different melodic elements float in and out of the mix.
‘Perception’ continues Sleepy & Boo’s long relationship with 3Bridge Records, and we’re thrilled to welcome the duo back to the catalog with this emotive and inspired release.

title: Evolutionary Tactics
review: Futureworlder is back on the label with two new heady slices of spaced-out ambient techno music, appropriately titled ‘Evolutionary Tactics’.

Part one takes everything we love about Brian’s productions and wraps them neatly into a nice headed-for-the stars package. Big expansive pads, racing hi-hats, melodic arpeggios, and tight drum programming are the main ingredients here. Part two is almost as if the mission is just about complete. Echoed radio speech, ethereal washes of sound, and an ambient ending as if the astronauts have landed…or not.
Launch yourself into the final frontier with this 2 tracker.

title: Dreaming Detroit
review: A new signing for the label, British producer Peter Ward lands with his single ‘Dreaming Detroit’ with a remix by 3Bridge favorite, Gatto and vocalist Bel Headspace.

The track is an exercise in classic house sounds with melodic stabs and pad progressions, thick bass lines, and snapping percussion. It has the sounds of older 808 State with an updated motif and it’s excellent. Gatto’s mix flips that on its head and creates a version with echoing analog splashes of sounds whirling about, big pads, bottom heavy percussion, and a latin flavored vocal by Bel Headspace.
Dream of Detroit with this great single.

tracks.title: Dreaming Detroit (Gatto I Can Hear You Detroit Mix featuring Bel Headspace)

title: Defective Metaphors
review: The Company Soundsystem (aka Alex Musto) returns to the label for his latest release ‘Defective Metaphors’. 3 jams on the dirty indie dance/tech house side of things, and the EP also includes a remix by label head Eric Shans.

‘Malicious Intent With Your Mind’ starts things off with a playful bass line, crystalline pads, and a breaks type beat along with some fun stream of consciousness dialog by vocalist H.A. Eugene over the course of it. Simply put, it’s a feel good, party track that will light up your dance floors. Eric’s remix takes it and turns it into a proper peak time banger with big analog bottom end, swirling melodies, and slick arpeggios. Next up is ‘We Want Revolutionaries’ and it takes vintage spoken word samples over grimy, driving beats, buzz-saw type bass lines, and afto-beat style percussion. And to close things out, ‘So Help Me God’ heads into after hours territory with twisted vocals, droning effected arpeggios, and energetic drums.

tracks.title: Malicious Intent With Your Mind feat. H.A. Eugene (Original Mix)
Malicious Intent With Your Mind feat. H.A. Eugene (Eric Shans Defective Remix)

title: L.O.V.E.
review: Label boss Deep Woods is back with a funky new deep house cut called ‘L.O.V.E.’ which comes just in time for the warmer spring months.

The original mix is a superb blend of disco-influenced goodness replete with groovy guitar licks, chunky bass lines, and a repeated simple vocal line. The deep mix goes for a little more tech based approach with smooth dub stabs, big drums, fat low end, and a wider vox treatment.
Get this new single and set your dance floors and rooftops on fire. Love is all we need.

title: Sleeping Giants
review: Frank Jackson (aka Gatto) comes back into 2020 on 3Bridge with ‘Sleeping Giants’, his latest collection of sweet electronic sounds. We’re super happy to be releasing this, and it immediately caught the attention of the label’s Creative Director, Eric Shans, when he heard it and well, we just had to put it out.

The title track cruises at a nice speed with pristine (and at times live sounding) percussion, a smooth bottom heavy low end, and hypnotic melodies that offer subtle changes in their chord progressions. Delayed vocal snippets float in and out as well and the synth riffs that punctuate them really give an expansive feel.

‘Sunrise’ is next and it pays a bit of homage to 90s ambient house music with the style of the of the crystal-ish sounding arpeggios all while a groovy bass line keeps the rhythms hinged to the beats. It’s one for the early mornings as the title depicts, or for that opening set where you’re starting to get people moving, and the rich analog textures in the track are really something to be heard.
Closing track is a bit of a remix of ‘Sleeping Giants’ but offers a little different take on the original blanketed in heavy synths, great drums, and constant movement.

title: Emerge
review: Sleepy & Boo are back on 3Bridge for the start of the new year and decade with their latest EP, ‘Emerge’. The New York-based duo has delivered three slices of top-shelf techno focused on those foggy rooms with big stacks of speakers, a powerful collection of music that sets a firm intention for 2020.

The title track ‘Emerge’ leads things off with an ominous hoover-esque bass line, driving highs, and deep chords that rip in and out of the percussion. A soft synth pad peeks its head in every now and again giving a melodic flourish over some of the percussive madness. This one is for the peak hours and the early mornings when the energy is on high.

‘Materialize’ is the second track and and it continues Sleepy & Boo’s appreciation for all things dub. They’ve crafted another dancefloor gem that is powered by deep stabs, ping ponging delays, and arpeggiated melodies, all anchored by a heavy percussive groove and cavernous atmospheres.

Closing this EP out is ‘Rise’, which is certain to leave a lasting impression on the crowd. Inspired by early Detroit vibes, this one mixes a deep and unforgettable melodic line with hypnotic synth stabs and arpeggiated analog leads. ‘Rise’ is all about the positive vibes that Sleepy & Boo create in their DJ sets, and has already gotten great reactions when played out.

We’re very excited to put this EP out to start the year strongly. This is Sleepy & Boo’s 7th EP on 3Bridge Records, and ‘Emerge’ demonstrates their continued evolution and expansion as producers. Happy new year!

title: The Best Of 3Bridge : 2019
review: It’s that time of year again around the holidays where we present a selection from each artist that has put out a track on the label this year. We hope you enjoy the collection with 3Bridge’s ever growing roster and diversity of sounds. We look forward to 2020!
