Eric Shans & Slav Ka - Red Moon (Original Mix)
The Company Soundsystem (feat Tarynn Hailey)- Through You (Original Mix)
Eric Shans - Out Of Sight (Original Mix)

title: Communication
review: We welcome a new signing for the last release on the label for 2019, Elliot DeHoyos. He brings us a 2 track EP that spans across the genres between melodic house and techno replete with expansive depth and layers.

‘Babel’ gives us some great dubbed chords, dreamy riffs, and rock solid percussion that will be able to shake any dance floor up. Vocoded, echoed voices float in and out of the mix too giving the track a bit of a retro-modern feel. This one is meant for the late nights and sunrise flooded mornings where the lights peeks through.

‘Subconscious Reality’ wraps the listener in deep house stabs, warm drifting melodies, celestial vocals, and blissful synthesizer workouts. Perfect for any deep house set, possibly for that transition period where both the music and people’s energy start to pick up.
3Bridge Records is finishing the year out strong with this big record. We hope you feel the same.

title: Memory Design
review: Futureworlder (aka Brian Traister) returns with his first release on 3Bridge in 2019. We’re delighted to be another one his works as he always delivers top quality and ‘Memory Design’ is no exception.

The title track coasts along with fat analog pads and melodies with shuffling hats, woodblocks, and claps serving as the rhythmic engine. Sparkling pads dialed up from the heavens shower the listener with sound and at the same time a chugging techno type bass line gives it some grit. There’s shadows of some of the best 808 State work here and fans of that sound would do well to seek this out.

‘Sumbawa’, which is an Indonesian island far far away from where the label is situated, is a real pretty number, it’s as if upon listening you’re flying over crystal blue waters as a metronomic heart beat pulses.
‘Fragments’ closes things out with a dash of acid combined with the trademark atmosphere we’ve come to know and love from this artist. Make this record a part of your memory.

title: Out Of Sight
review: Eric Shans returns to 3Bridge with ‘Out Of Sight’, his first original EP on the label this year. It’s a record that spans a few different styles and embodies Eric’s sound to a tee; the light meeting the dark and the space between those two opposites.

The title track starts things off on an upbeat note. Clean percussion drives the rhythms out of the gate coupled with a fat analog bass that moves things along nicely. The track builds around a progression where airy pads and arpeggios take the center stage. A simple vocal phrase repeats throughout and it’s nicely drenched in reverb to highlight the ethereal-ness of it. This is for the peak time hours and those sun drenched mornings or sunsets.

‘Line Of Fire’ is next and it’s a little deeper and darker with some superb low end, Persian style chants, and dub house chords all in the framework of a melodic house track. There’s some killer production on this one with lots of both atmospheric and rhythmic elements. Dance-able yet for the head and mind as well.

‘5AM Frames’ finishes the EP and goes into after hours minimal tech house territory with twisted vocals, effected synths & bass, strange arpeggios, and crunchy drums. It’s something you would hear probably well, at 5AM or some other crazy hour :). The breakdown in this one is pretty special too.
There’s a good variety of sounds to choose from on this EP – you’d do well to have them all in your crate.

title: Dreamers
review: 3Bridge mainstay Gatto is back on the label with a new EP and it’s a doozy; 3 great tracks of swirling, sweet goodness.

The title track kicks things off, and it has an interesting Kompakt-esque sound with a precisely EQ-ed kick, subtle but sharp hats, and layered percussion underneath. In line with the title, the pads and atmospheres are quite dreamy; perfect for a morning on the beach as the sun rises through the horizon, when you’re looking off of that rooftop into a glowing city skyline, or simply wanting to cast some chill sounds over people’s ears.

‘Waking Life’ harkens back to some of the sounds of the 90s ambient era with big ethereal synth riffs hovering over the fat bottom end of the track. Echoed and effected vocals rise and fall through the mix giving this a really shadowy, hazy feeling. It has a certain energy to it as well though, especially in its 2nd half.

The EP closes out with ‘Roll Play’ which ups the pace a bit with nicking hi-hats, tight snares and claps, and minor key stabs. Fitting with the rest of the record though, there’s a lot of atmosphere to it that sticks itself in like adhesive between the chugging bass and drums.
Immerse yourself with this great new EP. Mastered by Jeff Clarke at JC Mastering.

title: Someone To Luv
review: We’re delighted to have Riccicomoto (Enrico Regini) on the label again, this time with his own EP. Exquisitely produced, it’s 4 tracks that span the spectrum of genres of techno, dub, house, and electronica and features a remix by label head Eric Shans.

‘Someone To Luv’ starts things off and it’s a real trip into cavernous atmospheres, echoey vocals, and driving percussion. Soft dub sounds drift in and out, while big synth leads and beautiful pianos round out the track. The ‘Eric Shans Deep Hearts Mix’ takes a bit more of direct approach with his trademark analog sounding groovy bass lines, soundtrack-esque pads, and layered drums.

‘Take U Home (feat UK JOJO)’ brings down the BPMs a bit turning this into a smooth as silk soulful downtempo tune; it’s for those nights or mornings where you’re winding down, or just getting your day started.

‘Tetrahexagon’ explores the dub techno realm as if you were on a highway where the city horizon is glowing and breathing in the distance. Big beats hit against those trademark dub chords with a fat bottom end and interesting vocal samples.
Lastly ‘Trip With Me’ could serve as a backdrop for a science fiction video game or movie as interstellar riffs and vox are placed beneath racing hi hats and glitch vocal patterns.
Riccicomoto’s music really stands in a class of its own and you’d do well to pick up this EP which spans across many genres and sounds.

tracks.title: Someone To Luv (Eric Shans Deep Hearts Mix)
Take U Home (feat UK JOJO- Original Mix)

title: Drive Through The Crazy
review: Another new signing for 2019, we welcome The Company Soundsystem (aka Alex Musto) to 3Bridge Records. ‘Drive Through The Crazy’ is his newest offering and it features 3 original tracks, plus a remix by one of the 3Bridge captains, Eric Shans. ‘Through You feat. Tarynn Hailey’ starts things off and it takes a straight-ahead dirty, deep, tech house approach that aims straight for the dancers. A big bass riff and kick guide the proceedings here and piano type leads, random percussive elements, and Tarynn’s repeated vocal line are generously spread out in the mix. It also has a breakdown with an unexpected twist which will surprise you in the best way possible. It’s a track that could be played at any hour of the party. ‘Drive Me Crazy’ comes next and it’s an interesting meld of styles. Crunchy percussion, a fat bottom end, along with twisted vocal snippets guide the track along. Off-kilter arpeggios and synth swells blanket it with melodic twists and turns that play off of each other. The second version, the ‘Eric Shans Mental Health Mix’, is appropriately named. It ups the energy of the track frenetically with two bass riffs going back and forth coinciding with sharp racing hi-hats, distorted leads, and shuffling drums.

‘Pieces Of Meat, Waiting For A Butcher’ takes things into the deep end closing out the EP with a humungous low end, snares that smack away relentlessly, big synthesizer lines, and twisted movie samples. This is one for those late hours into the morning and it’s a real treat for the ears and the mind. Get yourself through the crazy and grab this EP for your sets. You’ll find plenty of reasons to play it. ‘Through You’ mixed and engineered by Tony Grund. EP mastered by Jeff Clarke.

tracks.title: Drive Me Crazy (Eric Shans Mental Health Mix)
Pieces Of Meat, Waiting For A Butcher (Original Mix)

title: Kaleidoscope
review: 3Bridge Records is very excited to welcome Begoña to the label with the release of her dynamic ‘Kaleidoscope EP’. Begoña is one half of 3Bridge mainstays and well-known NYC DJ and production duo Sleepy & Boo. ‘Kaleidoscope’ marks her first solo foray into the dance floor, featuring three tracks of melodic and lush atmospheres paired with hypnotic late-night grooves. She has already established herself as a producer on our sister label 3Bridge Elements, with two stellar chillout and downtempo EPs – both were met with critical acclaim and have been among the label’s best selling releases.

‘Mystic Rapture’ begins the EP on an uplifting and melodic note, and right away we’re treated to some truly inspiring sounds. This track is built around a beautiful chord progression which continually evolves throughout the journey. The energy builds and releases throughout, echoing a classic progressive style mixed with the dreamier soundscapes that Begoña is known for. This one is destined for some memorable dance floor moments.

Up next is ‘Prism’, which has been receiving a tremendous response in Begoña’s Sleepy & Boo DJ sets over the last few months. This track goes deep into a dub direction, mixing techy percussive grooves with heavy piano stabs, and a half-time rhythm that adds a refreshing element to the vibe. On top of it all is a haunting piano melody that really resonates in the mix. ‘Prism’ is a perfect example of the focus on this whole Kaleidoscope EP – a mix of different styles and sounds to represent the many colors on the underground spectrum.

Closing things out is ‘That Which Is Seen’ which takes a more drum-heavy, percussive focus before giving way to cascading arpeggios and melancholy minor progressions – the kind of deep and groovy afterhours track that induces late-night bliss and thoughtful contemplation. You can clearly hear the evolution from Begoña’s chillout productions to her dance floor direction with this solid closing track.
We’re very happy to have Begoña releasing her solo work on 3Bridge Records, and we’re eager to see what new sounds she continues to pursue.

title: Perseverance
review: New York mainstays Sleepy & Boo make their return to 3Bridge Records in 2019 with ‘Perseverance’. This is the duo’s seventh EP on the label, featuring three fresh tracks of melodic, uplifting grooves, the perfect material to ease the transition into the warmer spring months. It’s the follow-up to their last release – the ‘Return to Order EP’ – and we’re very excited to highlight Sleepy & Boo’s continued development and evolution as producers.

The lead track on the EP is ‘Persevere’, which sets the tone nicely for what’s to come. This one is prime dance floor material, and has been a staple in Sleepy & Boo’s sets for the last several months. It’s an optimal blend of melodic chord changes with a bottom-heavy percussive groove, and features several hands-in-the-air crescendos to set the dance floor off.

‘Seek’ is up next, and this composition ventures into more dreamy and introspective territory. Shuffling drums provide the foundation for crystalline piano riffs and soothing pads, another masterful fusion between musical and rhythmic elements. This track is a great choice for late nights and after hours mornings.

The final cut on the EP is ‘Persistence’, and it leaves us on a positive and thoughtful note. This track continues the themes established on the EP, mixing up chunky percussion with hypnotic, dubby chord stabs, analog bass lines, and swirling strings. Shimmering bells also lend a nice, rich color to this track, hinting at the optimism and spirit of the season to come.

We’re very happy to have Sleepy & Boo back on 3Bridge Records with this EP. They have been leaving their mark with a slew of new releases so far this year, including recent remixes for Intimate Project, Dark Beauty and Volante Records. Here’s to many happy dance floor moments to come, courtesy of ‘Perseverance’.

title: Connection Paths
review: For the 2nd release of 2019 on the label, we present to you label head Eric Shans teaming up again with Slav Ka (aka Slava Malkin) for a great EP on the techno end of the spectrum called ‘Connection Paths’. It takes Eric’s melodic sensibilities & affection for groovy, delicious beats along with Slav Ka’s razor sharp aural design, tweaked out soundscapes, and heady percussive workouts.

‘Flashpoint’ kicks things off and it’s a stormer of a track. A heavy kick drum and whip snares pound away, while deep dubbed chords stab rhythmically and acidic riffs cut in and out of the mix. It’s meant for that peak hour when people are sweatily dancing and smoke machines engulf the shadows. This one will surely stir up the energy on any given night.

‘Red Moon’ dials this energy down just a little but it’s no less captivating. Sci-fi sounds weave in between the minimal techno style beats, while big pads come later on launching the track into orbit, as if you were drifting away from planet earth into unknown and uncharted territory.

‘Receptors’ is hypnotic tech at its finest. Densely layered synth sounds create a thick atmosphere, often filtering in and out and morphing, while shuffling drum patterns glue the pieces together. It’s dark stuff without being brooding, a perfect backdrop to a dimly lit sky while the stars breathe in the distance, or an after hours room for the true music heads.
Connect your paths with this stunner of an EP.

title: Pressure
artistLine: Andres Luque, Deep Woods, Tony Crawm
review: We welcome back Spanish producer Tony Crawm (aka Antonio Laguna) back to 3Bridge Records for the first release of 2019. This time he is joined by another artist, Andres Luque. They’ve made something pretty spectacular and we’re really excited to put it out. It also features a remix by 3Bridge head honcho, Deep Woods (aka Greg Cuoco).

‘Pressure’ starts things right out of the gate with a groovy and consistent energy. Whipping percussion, brilliant synth workouts, and a catchy vocal scatters itself throughout. It’s meant for those fog riddled dance floors, both big and small where bodies are dancing in unison. There’s an old school house feel to the vocal as well which will win over both older and newer heads of the music.

‘Deeper Swamp’ keeps the energy going with another excellent vocal, soulful and mysterious. Racing hi-hats, great low end, and catchy melodies on the darker side outline the grooves. It’s an amalgam of the current tech house sound sprinkled with some 90s inspired percussion patterns that will get people moving.

The Deep Woods remix of ‘Pressure’ strips down the ideas a bit from the original and creates a rock solid groove where he overlays the vocal across a train of rhythms and sounds with his trademark atmospheric backdrops. It’s a great way to close things out.
Check out our first EP of 2019. We’re super happy with it and think you will be too.

title: The Best Of 3Bridge: 2018
review: The yearly greatest hits has become a tradition around the holidays here at 3Bridge Records. We present to you 10 hand picked tracks found on our releases from 2018. As always, we’re proud of all of the artists who have contributed to our catalog, and hope you enjoy the variety of sounds and styles we offer. Featuring Deep Woods, Eric Shans, Gatto, Simon Sampler, Weston Butler, Mark Ryal, Eisenheim with Mel Pómene, Gianni Ruocco & Le Roi Carmona, Connie Yin & Nora Nostrand, and Futureworlder.

title: Warriors
review: We’re happy to have Gatto (aka Frank Jackson) with his first release on the label this year. His new EP ‘Warriors’ pays homage to the older days of New York City ( where the 3Bridge is based) and does so in a high quality way.

‘Crossing The Bridge’ starts this EP off racing out of the gate. Fat dub chords with incredibly groovy patterns and drums are the main ingredients here along with ride cymbals, and fast paced hi hats adding the accents to the track. It makes this a really playable jam any time of the night or day.

Next track ‘Da Bronx’ kicks off with a funky, live sounding huge bass line that’s replete with tight danceable percussion and grooves. Repeated vocal chants give it a throwback deep house feel and you picture yourself traveling on the rumbling subway through the streets while the beats pump through your speakers or headphones.
‘We The People’ slows down the pace a bit with soft pads and synth lines while drum sounds pack a meaty punch. Both versions are a great closer to a wonderful EP.

title: Zabriskie Point
review: The duo of Gianni Ruocco and Le Roi Carmona are back on 3Bridge with their new single ‘Zabriskie Point’ and like their last release, it features a remix by label head Eric Shans.

The original mix is a straight ahead melodic house groover.. A pizzicato type lead takes the track at the helms guiding us through the melodic structure. Beefy kick drums and tough bass lines provide a bit of a rugged undercurrent similar to the landscape at Zabriskie Point, while the overall energy level of the track keeps things at a pumping pace.

The ‘Eric Shans Above The Valley Remix’ adds a bit of layering to the chord progression with big strings, pads, and percussion. It’s appropriately named as it’s as if one is floating above the hot depths of the Death Valley (Zabriskie Point) terrain. It’s almost has a soundtrack type quality that is moving and majestic.
On a beach, in a club, or an intimate setting, this single would work for every scenario. Don’t miss it.

tracks.title: Zabriskie Point (Eric Shans Over The Valley Remix)

title: Broken Path EP
review: We welcome another addition to the 3Bridge family, NYC DJ and producer Weston Butler. His EP ‘Broken Path’ is a gem and we’re happy to be putting it out.

Slight progressive undertones highlight the title track with melodic synths cascading over each other while sharp claps and hats provide the metronome to euphoric highs and lows throughout. Echoed voices smattered with delay swim under the surface, coming up for air every so often. There’s shadows of the progressive sound of yesteryear and pays homage to tracks heard on the older Renaissance and Global Underground compilations.

‘Angie’ follows a similar format, but the dreaminess is taken up a notch. The track builds up with beautiful layers of synth pads and leads. You could picture hearing this at a sunrise on the beach, or that final track in the morning at a party where everyone has danced the night away and maybe even have fallen in and out of love. It’s a fitting closer and brings the point of the title of the EP home; it’s as if you’ve might have found your way at the end of your journey.
Don’t miss this EP, it’s something special. Look for more from this up-and-coming producer.

title: Core, Pt. 3: Consciousness
review: We welcome another new signing for the label for 2018, this time it’s Mexico City based artist Eiesenheim (aka Irving Castillo). What really struck us about these productions is their complex melodic overtones, subtle grooves, and musical quality.

The first track ‘Telemetry Ft. Mel Pómene.’ takes beautiful pianos, synth leads, and bass lines, and melds them together with tight grooves and percussion. There’s enough infectious hooks in here that will keep people’s interest intact and the beauty of the piece is that it could be played in an opening set, or at peak time. A colorful tapestry weaves it all together making it a real winner of a track. The Deep Woods remix takes those elements and ups the funk a bit, driving the drums a bit with a harder smack; very much inline with his sound as of late.

‘Coda’ keeps Eisenheim’s ear for cinematic approaches grounded as squelchy acid type bass plays under the chord progressions anchored by shuffling hats, kick drums, and claps. There’s a element of fantasy in the piece of well, picture big forests with a mountainous backdrop all the while people dancing in unison and sun and clouds fight for space in the sky.
Heavily atmospheric and at the same time groove laden, you won’t want to miss this EP.

title: Hold On To Me EP
review: We’re happy to present one of the 3Bridge Records label heads, Eric Shans’ new release- the ‘Hold On To Me EP’. And proudly, we welcome the fantastic producer Riccicomoto (aka Enrico Regini) to the label offering 2 amazing remixes, as well as vocalist Uliya who’s featured on the track ‘Move’.

‘Hold On To Me’ is a real exercise in melody driven deep house. Analog chord sequences, rhythmic vocal snippets, and a slick bottom end are the main drivers here. It’s a track that’s meant to be played for sunset, desert sunrises, beach days, or at a crystal blue pool. The main vocal hook is a Persian-type chant, which is what the title is based on. Eric’s trademark approach to composing ethereal, melodic groovers is in full throttle here making you dance and at the same time dream. Riccicomoto’s mix slows down the pace and creates a beautiful cavernous tapestry of sound with deep, dubbed chords, effected voices, and stellar sound design.

‘Out Of My Mind’ ups the tempo a bit and it is simply captivating in its’ wistfulness and endearing sounds. Both new romantic and melancholy (often a trademark in Eric’s productions), it layers melody with grace and effortlessness along with a driving beat and bass line with vox samples that strike through the heart. Riccicomoto’s version takes the song and adds even more vocals and classical type instrumentation and it has an almost neo-soul approach with an absolutely beautiful Balearic atmosphere; one of those songs that would be perfect for lazy mornings and nights with a lover or friends, or late night drives with starry skies. Distant violins, fuzzy arpeggios, and outer space synth sounds fly in and out of the mix slowly and effectively.

Balancing the new romantic and melancholy (often a trademark in Eric’s productions), the track layers melody with grace and effortlessness along with a driving beat and bass line with vocal samples that strike through the heart. Riccicomoto’s version takes the song and adds even more vocals and instrumentation, delivering an almost neo-soul approach with an absolutely Balearic beautiful atmosphere; one of those songs that would be perfect for lazy mornings and nights with a lover or friends, or late night drives with starry skies. Distant violins, fuzzy arpeggios, and outer space synth sounds fly in and out of the mix slowly and effectively.

To conclude on a groovy note ‘Move’ features the vox of Uliya and it’s a funky tech house romp. It will get you up and on a dance floor as dirty bass lines, big house hits, and subtle melodic riffs play off each other while the shuffling tough percussion and a simple vocal refrain that tells you to move, and to not overthink it.
This is a stunning new EP from one of the 3Bridge Records captains, one you won’t want to miss.

tracks.title: Hold On To Me (Riccicomoto Deep Session
Out Of My Mind (Riccicomoto Soul Session)

title: Beef And Granny EP
review: Simon Sampler returns to 3Bridge with his release, the ‘Beef And Granny EP’. We’ve always liked Simon’s work a whole lot and this time around, he has 2 quirky tracks to unleash that are meant for those late club nights.

‘Beef Dito’ starts things off with a bouncy huge kick drum and slick techno type percussion with a repeated vocal sample throughout that becomes a part of the rhythm after time. A Giorgio Moroder type bass line causes the low end waves to ebb and flow while twisted synth riffs enter in and out of the spectrum. It’s sure to get a dance floor moving and the unique sound of it will captivate the ears.

‘Granny Smith’ still keeps the theme of twisted, deep tech house but this one is a bit of a slower burn and tempo. Filthy bass riffs compliment the kick and clap, and some fun vocal samples are scattered throughout. It’s minimal in its presentation and the restraint here is the strength, using each element and placing them carefully in the mix.
And without further ado, give these tracks a spin. You’ll be glad you did.

title: Snow Dream EP
review: Futureworlder is back on 3Bridge in 2018 with his newest offering, the ‘Snow Dream’ EP. It makes sense that the release is right of the middle of the winter on the east coast which has been wrought with snow and cold. That said, there are plenty of warm, bright melodies in this EP that will make you wish you were on an apex somewhere overlooking a beautiful landscape of sugary snow capped mountains.

The title track coasts along with Futureworlder’s trademark percussion style; racing 16th notes, a fat kick drum, and reverb heavy claps serve as the drivers while huge analog pads create dramatic high notes. Immerse yourself in this one, you’ll picture yourself skiing down a breezy slope, while pine trees and cozy cabins pass by you. Eric’s remix of it takes the melodic elements and adds a few different arpeggios, a house-influenced bass line, and even more effected layers to tie it all together.

‘An Open Window’ takes a similar approach to ‘Snow Dream’ but dials down the energy just a tad to make this more of a reflective track. Shimmering symphonic chords wash over the groovy percussive work outs and bass, giving this a truly ambient techno feel. And ‘Empathy’ goes deeper into the tech influenced music you can tell Brian truly has affection for. Heavy kick drums, a distant snare, and flashes of 90s electronica are the main sound players here all while still latching on to the melodic theme that this EP has throughout.
Close your eyes and drift into a ‘Snow Dream’ with this EP.

tracks.title: Snow Dream (Eric Shans Blizzard Drifts Remix)

title: Owls
review: For our first release of 2018, we present the head of 3Bridge Records newest creation, the ‘Owls’ EP. Partially a concept work, it’s 3 slices of heady, deep tech house that create beautiful atmospheres. Each track highlights a different owl and builds the music around them.

Leading the sequence, ‘The Barn Owl’ chugs along with racing hi-hats, tech-laden percussion, and sparkling leads that coast over the terrain of moody pads and sublime sounds. This would be work great as a late night track as fog lights encompass a dance floor or in the scene of a fantasy type film where sunlight pokes through the dark forests where creatures wait and observe their surroundings.

‘The Great Horned Owl’ takes things in a bit more of a darker direction. It’s known that this breed are strong predators, feeding on an amalgam of other animals. and you get the sense hearing the tone of the track as if you might be running from one (as a small animal) or observing a parliament of them having some sort of group ritual. You’ll hear their chants scattered here too as the song builds and morphs.

Lastly, ‘The Screech Owl’ is almost a combination of the first 2 tracks, blending ethereal elements, tribal type drums, and echoed string riffs. Their vocals are here too if you were ever curious how they sound.
Owls are a mythical type bird and this Deep Woods EP perfectly captures their aesthetic with these 3 great pieces.

title: The Best Of 3Bridge 2017
review: It’s been a great year here at 3Bridge Records and in keeping with our yearly tradition, we’ve hand picked 11 tracks from this year’s releases and present to you them as individual tracks and an album only DJ mix. It’s no easy task going through each one and selecting what we love the most as we’re very proud of all of them. We’d like to take this opportunity to thank each artist for their hard work and the excellent music they’ve given us to put out. Enjoy!

title: Another World EP
review: For one of the last releases of the year, we bring you a special treat – music by the duo of Slav Ka and Eric Shans. It’s the first time ever the two have worked on music together (besides Eric’s remixing of his track ‘Endless’) and the results are something really cool and unique. Three tech induced workouts all with a different flavor. Title track “Another World” starts off things with an upbeat, driving tempo replete with a fat bass line, distorted arpeggios and subtle pads that swim beneath its interstellar surface. The shuffling percussion keep the rhythm driving while echoes of the dark progressive sound of the early 2000s play on its backbone. That said, it’s got a lot of modern twists and turns which make it really stand out. ‘Space Lullaby’ is next up with some fun vintage dialogue as well as some ethereal sci-fi atmospheres, coupled with some acid techno riffs that slice through the mix. It has a bit of a minimal structure however there’s layers that crawl and breathe under the heady percussion that shine through like spiraling headlights in the darkness. ‘One Night In Kiev’ (the title reflects the fact that Slav Ka is in fact, Ukranian) dials down the energy just a bit closing things out with a solid groove. A fat kick drum and bass launch this one into motion while soaring arpeggiated pads weave in and out of the night scape. Subtle and melodic, it’s sure to raise ears on the dance floor. Perfect for the coming winter months, this EP would be a great collection for DJs looking for tech-laden, danceable tracks for their crates.

title: Return To Order EP
review: Sleepy & Boo make their return to 3Bridge Records with their second label EP of 2017, the three-track ‘Return to Order EP’. This release is one of the duo’s most accomplished works yet, a shimmering collection of uplifting and melodic gems that are sure to create long-lasting dancefloor memories. We’re very excited to welcome them back with this expertly crafted EP, highlighting a new dimension to Sleepy & Boo’s evolving sound.

The title track ‘Return to Order’ has its genesis in the eighth meditation sound path that Begoña of Sleepy & Boo has been creating over the last year. Its melody is a haunting guitar loop that conjures up a dreamy morning groove, anchored by a hypnotic bassline and upfront, precise percussion. As dubbed-out, delayed stabs and warm pads are introduced, the track builds to an ethereal crescendo. ‘Return to Order’ has been a staple of Sleepy & Boo’s sets over the last few months, with partygoers routinely approaching the booth for a track ID when they hear it.

Up next we have ‘Glimmer’, a composition that delves deep into emotional atmospheres and textures. This track is driven by a powerful chord progression that strengthens and evolves as it moves forward. There’s a peak-hour, hands-in-the-air break, as soaring arpeggios and vocal samples intensify the energy for a true goosebump-inducing experience.

Wrapping up this release is ‘White Light’, which weaves the melodic themes of the previous two tracks into a tight, techno-flavored, late-night workout. Rolling basslines, filtered analog synths, hypnotic notes, and an extended keyboard solo are some of the most prominent elements of the track, making it an ideal selection for DJs looking for a unique and moody pick to stand out in their set.

title: Checkmate EP
review: Gatto (aka Frank Jackson) returns to 3Bridge for his 2nd release of 2017. It’s an EP of meticulously programmed tech house meant for those dark fog machine riddled dance floors.

‘Rumble’ kicks things off with typewriter type mechanical rhythms that drive the track while effected synths rise and fall out of the mix. There’s a very well known spoken word sample in here which people might recognize, and it adds a sense of fun to the proceedings. It’s a stomper of a song and will get people moving. The ‘Bad Ass Beats Mix’ uses a bit of a different sound palette but it’s no less energetic. There’s a homage to older techno here, note the sequenced whistles that happen during it. Tribal type percussion is the main ingredient here, with a groovy bass line intact.

Title track ‘Checkmate’ has a bit of 2000s Bedrock sound to it with more updated sounds and structures. Cleanly programmed drums propel it forward while sprinkles of atmospheric synths, peppered with claps and fills keep the energy going. A melodic hook pulls you in and doesn’t let go until the end.
This EP is essential for anyone’s crate, regardless of the style you play.

title: Who Will Save Us EP
review: Originally a B-side on the ‘Gone Away EP’, Eric Shans’ track ‘Who Will Save Us’ was quite well received when it was released, so we felt it needed more attention and a re-release on the label. We’re happy to present it once again.

The original mix and title track is a mountainous groovy melodic boomer with harmonized vocals that expand across the sky. Mournful but at the same time uplifting (a staple theme in Eric’s productions), it packs a huge bass with crispy tight, drums and has lit up dance floors across the NY scene. The ‘When We Fall Remix’ (done by Mr Shans himself) takes a bit of a darker turn, but eventually the fog clears and the track picks up where the original left off, this time with a more sub sounding bass line, moodier pads, and added vox. It’s quite a journey. And the last remix by NYC producer and DJ, Tristan Dominguez, marries percussive grooves with a tough low end all leading to an angelic breakdown as if the heavens open up and stop time before getting back into motion.

The closer ‘On Your Own’ is dialed down dreamy deep house with a soulful repeating vocal phrase that hooks you in. It’s an emotional end to the EP and its strings that sound like ending credits to a film coast over the drums and bass line, ultimately lifting it up into the clouds.
Who will save us from ourselves? Pick up this EP and find out.

tracks.title: Who Will Save Us (Tristan Dominguez Remix)

title: Lost People EP
review: One of our favorite producers on 3Bridge, Roberto Pedoto comes back with this great little EP. His unmistakable deep house style is in full force here, delivering 2 great originals plus a remix by Soul Trader that takes Roberto’s style and morphs it into total energetic techno.

‘Everything Changes’ starts things off in true Roberto fashion. A buttery, funky bassline sits below sharp hats and drums, while layered synth stabs oscillate back and forth. Echoed soulful vocals rise and fall out of the mix giving the track a human touch. It’ll move a dance floor, for sure. British producer Soul Trader (aka Adam Walder) takes the track and flips it upside down throttling the energy and pace, transforming it into a late night banger. You want a track to drop at 4am to make people lose their minds? Look no further, you have your solution right here.

Closer and title track ‘Lost People’ has a 90s house influence with a gentle chord progression with stabs, quiet strings, and delayed vocal phrases over a stellar percussion pattern. It’s meant for both poolsides and the transition period at a party where people started to get warmed up to the DJ’s grooves for the night.
We’re happy to be putting out more music from this great Italian producer and we also welcome Soul Trader to the label as well!

title: Can’t Stop EP
review: We welcome another addition to the 3Bridge roster for 2017, Ukranian producer DJ Lutique. When we got these demos, we were immediately hooked and excited to put them out. 3 tracks of deep, banging, funky tech house just in time for your summer parties.

Take a listen to the sounds on ‘Can’t Stop’ – driving percussion coupled with a soulful bassline and leads really make this one for the dance floor. Repeated vocal chops come in and out propelling the rhythms giving the track an undeniable energy. ‘Got The Love’ follows a similar formula, but goes a little into more tech territory with dotted chord hits, big ride cymbals, crunchy percussion, and vocoded warped voices. Underneath it all, there’s real soul in it though suited to get bodies moving and shaking. And ‘Make It Hot’ closes things out, another example of Lutique’s party focused musical attitude and style. A peak time banger that will light the club up.
We can’t stop listening to the ‘Can’t Stop EP’ and you’ll have a whole lot of fun with this one.

title: Safeless EP
review: Austria based producer Simon Sampler strikes back with his first release on the label for 2017, the ‘Safeless EP’. It’s 2 tracks that encompass the best parts of groove laden techno.

‘Safeless’ is a real stomper; huge drums undercut with a thick analog bass line bringing a smattering of filth to it. Sequenced blips and bleeps take us for the ride through this journey but make no mistake, there’s soul in the machine here and the sounds never get to be too overbearingly mechanical. It’ll satisfy tech-house and techno fans alike as it straddles the line of both genres perfectly.

‘Unda Ground’ dials down the energy just a bit but carries some of the same characteristics of the previous track. Funky, fun, and a little twisted, smoldering dirty low end and tight drum programming drive this one, and in conjunction with off-kilter synth riffs and vocals, it gives the piece an overall edgy, meaty sound. Top quality stuff.
Simon is continuously creating quality music and we’re really happy to be putting this record out.

title: My Funky Bitch EP
review: Gatto, aka Frank Jackson, returns to 3Bridge Records with a fantastic second release, the ‘My Funky Bitch EP’ and it also features a remix by one of the label’s co-captains, Eric Shans.

The title track is a bit of a throwback to the days of progressive breaks. A rolling thick bass line guides the rhythm as layered percussion shuffles and shakes through it, while smooth driving effected pads coast on top. It’s almost a soundtrack to a video game that takes place sometime in the distant future where you are the driver of of a spaceship funkily moving through time and space. The second half changes things up as the beats take a 4/4 approach; it’s unexpected and will bring a smile.

The ‘Eric Shans Stole The Money remix’ takes a different angle – it delves into the sounds of deeper tech while keeping the main riffs of the original as its guide. Fat house stabs with filtered acidic lines keep the momentum strong and these are punched between the wide kick and claps. It’s a great compliment to the original and would completely work on a dancefloor.

‘Soul Grabber’ rounds off this EP and it does it in stylistic tech-house fashion. Soulful vocal loops play over the tough beats and bass lines while arpeggiated synths swim in and out gluing the foundation of it. This would work as a peak time or warm up track; it straddles that line perfectly.
Make sure you pick up Gatto’s new release – you’ll be sure to have a blast with it.

tracks.title: My Funky Bitch (Eric Shans Stole The Money Remix)

title: The Surrender EP
review: We’re super excited to be putting out Sleepy & Boo’s first 3Bridge release of 2017. The New York-based duo released four great EPs with the label last year, as well as a killer remix, and ‘The Surrender EP’ is no exception to their prolific and growing catalog of quality dancefloor music.

Title track ‘The Surrender’ starts us off and it’s a melodic builder of euphoric dimensions, designed to inspire rooms both big and small for hands-in-the-air moments in the midst of those late nights and early mornings. A massive kick and clap coasts in tandem with the the crisply programmed hi-hats, while an airy, elegant chord progression builds. Huge pads and choirs drive right through the heart of this track in an almost kaleidoscopic fashion. Colorful, driving, otherworldly, and anthemic at all once, you will surely want this one for your sets.

‘Cycles Of Time’ goes for a bit of a more understated, groove-building approach. Dubbed out chords, swirling vocal samples and swinging, slick percussion are the emphasis here, sitting nicely above a solid kick. Rich layers of synth melodies arrive later in the track, inspiring the dancefloor to look skyward. This one conjures visions of the sun setting over the horizon on a hazy summer day, or the morning light peeking through a warehouse roof.

Wrapping up this EP is ‘Yield’. Here you have a great juxtaposition of ethereal riffs and sequencing, blended with acidic bass lines that filter in and out throughout the course of the track. Truly a paradox of gritty and dreamy, it’s a great end to the EP and a nice way to encapsulate the dynamics of Sleepy & Boo’s production repertoire.

‘The Surrender EP’ is pure class, embodying elements of sophisticated melodies and dancefloor friendly workouts. Sleepy & Boo continue to deliver outstanding work, and we at 3Bridge Records could not be happier about it.

title: A Stranger To Ourselves EP
review: A funny thing happened when Greg (Deep Woods) and Eric were sharing creations back and forth recently, they realized they used the same vocal sample independently on a track. This sparked the idea that they’d do a split EP together and it was also chance for both of them to put music out that went into the deeper, darker side. Eric had a few tracks that were done but not released, as did Greg. And the end result is the ‘A Stranger To Ourselves’ EP.

Eric’s version of ‘A Stranger To Ourselves’ has a lot of elements of techno and grooves along with a bumping bass line, slick drums, and arpeggios filtering in and out poking melodic holes in the heady atmosphere. Later on, choirs bring out a haunting yet uplifting melody as the echoed main vocal repeats itself. To contrast, Deep Woods’ version hammers away with tribal house elements and organic jungle sounding synth workouts as the main elements. It’s a dark journey and one to really experience as a listener; it transports you to another dimension. It’s as if both versions are set in different locales – the reaches out of outer space, and the innards of a forest, fitting each artist respectively.

‘Into The Room’, by Eric takes a complete hairpin turn from his usual melodic delivery and the result is a spooky, booming tech house track, with thick bass lines, rugged percussion, and meaty lead synths. There’s an overall sense of devious fun to the track without being too brooding; it’s the aural equivalent of watching a campy horror movie that you can dance to.

‘Truly A Miracle’ comes next from Mr Woods, and it’s a perfect follow up to ‘Into The Room’. It has a distinct after hours vibe for those early mornings and late nights. Smacking drums and a healthy low-end are the main ingredients here coupled with some sinister riffs that stay in line with the main grooves.

The last 2 tracks lighten up the mood a bit. ‘Fire Breather’ is flooded with smooth pads that ebb and flow, while tinges of acid add some grit – it counterpoints some of the ominous sounds heard earlier on the EP. But it still keeps it a bit twisted with chopped vocals and warped 80s sounding synthesizer lines. And to end, ‘Then Again Who Does’ has a familiar sample from a famous sci-fi that you might recognize. Square low-end and nice pads and strings take us through the dialed down beats and echoed thuds that pass through the colorful spectrum.
Don’t be a stranger and pick up this EP from the 3Bridge Records captains.

tracks.title: A Stranger To Ourselves (Eric Shans Science Or Fiction Mix)
A Stranger To Ourselves ( Deep Woods Mix)

title: Old Tech
review: Rick Wade, one of our favorite producers across the board comes into 2017 with another release on the label. Originally slated for last year, but out now, ‘Old Tech’ is a rock solid house jam, replete with dubbed chords, racing hi hats, and supreme grooves to get a dance floor shaking. There’s some old school techno flavor, along with Chicago house, and it’s everything we’d expect from Mr. Wade, a known staple in the electronic music world. Label co-captain, Eric Shans also does his take on the track, adding a bit of a different melodic flavor to the proceedings while keeping the energy and flow of the original intact. Smooth, pretty pads decorate the crisp hi hats, while a big kick drum and fat bass line drive the shuffling percussion. The start of 2017 has 3Bridge Records looking bright.

title: Sunspots EP
review: For the start of 2017, we welcome Futureworlder ( aka Brian Traister ) to the label. Brian has been producing music for quite some time now and it’s all pretty brilliant if we do say so ourselves. Appropriately titled lead track ‘Sunspots’ is 7+ minutes of melodically rapturous techno. Cinematic in its approach yet danceable, deep lush pads build and layer over each other as if you were stacking them on top of one another to climb to the heavens. A silky thick bass, punchy kick, and sharp hi-hats with 16th notes grounding the patterns; all resulting in a hypnotic beat driven haze. ‘Other Methods’ takes a bit of a different angle with a Giorgio Moroder-esque lead and dubbed out delayed chords. A simple melody comes in and out playing over the kick, clap, and sub-bass giving it a refined sound. ‘Spectrum Analysis’ plays like ‘Sunspots’ cloudier sibling, but it’s no less euphoric with its sweeping tsunami like waves of beauty washing over the listener. And ‘Things Imminent’ is a meditative track of sorts, making us reflect on the many things this EP makes you feel. A definite throwback and a to classic ambient music both in its sound design and form – it’s a perfect closer. Get closer to the sun and bliss out with Futureworlder’s debut EP on 3Bridge.

title: The Grandmother Pie
review: Ukrainian producers the Brocartel strike back with a vengeance on their new single ‘The Grandmother Pie’. Funny enough, there’s some real irony in the title in that there’s very little that’s sugary about it – it’s a dirty, groovy, funky tech house jam that will get people really moving.

The original version is one of those pieces that will instantly pique the ears of dance floor revelers. A main vocal sample plays over the tough beats, and a wickedly filthy bass line really drives it along, and random percussive elements with pads dip in and out; all micro programmed for maximum effect.

Label captains, Deep Woods and Eric Shans also give their own take on the track. ‘Eric’s Cherry Custard Remix’ adds some spooky atmospheres to the offering with his own unmistakable dirtiness as well, and Mr. Woods offers a bit more energy in his remix, guaranteed to light the fire higher in the clubs where ‘The Grandmother Pie’ gets cooked.
Our last release of 2016 and it’s a great one. Don’t miss out on it.

tracks.title: The Grandmother Pie (Eric's Cherry Custard Mix)

title: Thought Forms EP
review: 2016 has been a banner year for New York producers Sleepy & Boo, with the duo releasing quite a bit of quality music. This is their 4th EP out this year on 3Bridge, and they have continuously impressed the label with solid dance floor tracks featuring a variety of styles and sounds. The ‘Thought Forms EP’ is no exception, and it’s perfect for your autumn DJ sets.

Opener ‘Thought Form’ is a great slice of house that takes the melodies deep and lush, crafting an irresistible, enveloping warmth that sets the stage for this accomplished EP. A thick kick drum that’s backed by crisp hi-hats and concordant dubbed patterns are the main drivers here, while wide tuneful pads cast a musical net that weaves in and out of focus. A moody chord progression ties all of this together, creating an uplifting atmosphere.

‘The Imaginary Past’ brings the clouds in a little bit, heading things down a darker direction. Large layers of arpeggios build over the course of the track, with haunting atmospheres descending throughout. This track puts the percussion up front, with filtered drums crunching and clicking in the background – including a vintage breakbeat loop. This is a perfect selection for those late night sets.

‘Process’ follows some of the same ideals as the previous track with catchy rhythms floating over echoing voices, soft stabs, and tough drums. It accurately reflects the NYC sound of today, which balances a rugged groove with melodic moments. Sleepy & Boo are mastering this to a tee, as this EP proudly represents

title: Naked Feet In Sand EP
review: We welcome NYC producer, Shakib Jakir, to the 3Bridge roster with his stunning EP, ‘Naked Feet In Sand’. Darkly atmospheric, driving, and funky are the main ingredients here, and these are meant to be played in dimly lit rooms, late at night. Title track ‘Naked Feet In Sand’ starts things off with a twisted lead riff that contain some elements of older Bedrock sounding progressive house over the top of a groovy bass line and solid percussion. Melodies build on top of each other and drift in and out, creating a heady aural palette for your ears while you take in its beats. ‘Diamond Dogs’ brings the same characteristics but ups the energy a bit – you could picture this being played dancing under a night sky with its twinkling starry like synths, and thick atmospheres that catapult you into another world for its duration. Appropriately titled ‘At The End’ concludes this 3 track, and comes at us with slick crisp drums, a brooding melody, and a female vocal that really drive this EP home. A knack for creating music on the haunting side of things but not any less playable, Shakib is a producer who is one to watch. We’re proud to release his very first EP to the world.

title: Brooklyn, NY
artistLine: Deep Woods, Rick Wade, Sleepy & Boo
review: Label head Deep Woods welcomes in the autumn season with a new single that is about his (and 3Bridge’s coincidentally) current residence, ‘Brooklyn, NY’. Taking his funky house approach with his trademark techy sound, this is sure to light up a dance floor. It’s also bit of a social commentary on how popular the borough has become over the past decade. Old time vocal recordings provide snippets of dialogue over floating synth lines while shuffling, pristine percussion provide lots of movement and danceability.

Detroit master Rick Wade’s version takes the track into deeper territory with darker pads and atmospheres, it’s almost as if you can see the borough’s skyline drenched in twilight. A mysterious melody is the main backbone here against the groove. There’s plenty of rhythm here to go around to get people moving but also would work in a more laid back setting.

And lastly, NYC producers Sleepy & Boo provide their take on the single by giving it a heady after hours feel, with lush stabs, crisp hats, a bottom heavy kick, and tough rhythms. They’ve also modeled the dialog snippets in their remix in a way which is enormously fitting: ‘Brooklyn..never sleeps’. Given the amount of night life that has migrated to Brooklyn in the past few years, it’s quite a true statement.
Get yourselves acquainted with ‘Brooklyn, NY’ with this great piece of work.

title: In The Moment EP
review: New York City mainstays Sleepy & Boo are back with their third EP of 2016 on 3Bridge Records, the ‘In The Moment’ EP. The duo has once again crafted three great pieces of work, each with varying sounds and approaches to their dance floor-based productions.

The title track ‘In The Moment” has been tested on dance floors around the world by Sleepy & Boo all summer, and we’re very excited to drop this one. The track is a dub-influenced dance floor workout, built around a solid bass line and percussive elements. Ethereal pads and dubbed out vocal samples build to a crescendo of arpeggiated leads and a massive bass wobble that makes the crowd erupt. It’s a really nice journey that will have you wanting more at the end. ‘Transform’ follows some of the same motif; the percussion swings on this one a bit more, with just as much tunefulness and groove. An especially catchy old-school house piano and soothing chords on top of it all gives the track a warm and uplifting vibe. ‘Completely Chosen’ rounds things off, veering on the more techno side of the spectrum with punchy chord stabs and subtle melody peppered over the tough sequencing and filtering heard throughout.
Get yourself captured ‘In The Moment’ with this release from Sleepy & Boo.

title: Deep Twist
review: Another new signing for the label for 2016, we’re proud to present 3 tracks of deep/tech house goodness from NY producer Gatto (aka Frank Jackson). The title track starts things off, and it’s a solid groover, taking a chunky bass line and bumping percussion that fills out the bottom half of track while subtle touches of melody and texture ebb and flow over the top of it. Safe to say it would fit in any set, regardless of style. ‘Take A Ride’ uses a galloping type riff that’s reminiscent of Giorgio Moroder with synth stabs, fun sound effects, and punchy drums that will get you moving. And ‘Out On The Tiles’ takes things a bit deeper and darker, rounding out this EP nicely with some melancholic guitars and rhythms.
The ‘Deep Twist’ EP is another example of the ever growing talented roster we have here at 3Bridge Records.

title: That Cat
review: For the first time ever, 3Bridge Records label heads Deep Woods (aka Greg Cuoco) and Eric Shans have teamed up for their release of a single called ‘That Cat’. It only made sense for the two to collaborate on this project since they both are big fans of felines as well. But the track is not really about cats, it’s based around an interesting and hilarious phone message left many years ago on an answering machine to get on the guest list for one of the legendary Aqua-Booty! parties in NYC that Greg used to help curate.

Both versions have similar aspects and patterns – groovy house chords with solidly layered percussion, melodic undertones, along with the vocal sample that has to be heard to be believed. These would go well in any sort of set, at any time of the night or day. The chunky pounce of the ‘Meow Mix’ and the playful twists of the ‘Frisky Mix’ really make this single a winner. And the acapella is the original phone message that was left so use it in your tracks!
3Bridge is proud to put out the first release from this duo and it definitely won’t be the last.

title: Sidewinder
review: Just in time for summer, Eric Shans’ single ‘Sidewinder’ is another demonstration of his ability to craft interesting dance music for your ears and your legs. This single also includes the always solid and inventive producer Pete Schwinge on remixing duties.

The ‘Original Mix’ uses a warm sub bass line as its core and creates fun, twisted melodies and synth workouts around it. House stabs, quirky vocal samples, and thick percussive elements drive the track, making it a tech-house romp that will bring smiles to those dancers faces. The ‘Scrambler Mix’ goes for more the straight ahead (but no less unique) direction with drifting analog pads and sophisticated driving rhythms. And with the ‘Buzz Motif Mix’, Schwinge brings his own musicality into the the track with great production techniques and pristine sequencing that ultimately peaks with a ‘hands in the air’ crescendo that will leave people wanting more.
Take a ride on the ‘Sidewinder’.

title: The Innocent EP
review: New York City producers Sleepy & Boo return to 3Bridge Records with their second release, ‘The Innocent EP’. These three tracks showcase their deeper, more melodic side, and it’s a great counterpoint to ‘The Capability EP’ that was released in March. This EP highlights their diversity as producers, and it drops right in time to welcome the warmer months of Summer ahead.

Lead track ‘Innocent’ is an anthemic instant classic, with a steady percussive flow, and subtle melodic chord and bass changes throughout. Strings and synth leads shine on the top end and eventually the track builds into a colossal, beautiful number that will have everyone on the dance floor cheering and hollering for more. This track has been met with rapturous response in all of Sleepy & Boo’s recent sets. ‘Humble’ straddles the line between deep house and techno, with filtered out tinges of acid-touched riffs, classic house pads, and echoed vocals that propel it forward. And ‘Overcome’ is replete with a dreamy aural palette, paradoxically stacked against fast-paced arpeggios that create great movement and rhythm. For prime-time dancefloors and afterhours alike, ‘The Innocent EP’ is a solid addition to the 3Bridge Records catalog and Sleepy & Boo’s discography.

title: Germany
review: Techno producer Tony Crawm is back with his first release on 3Bridge for 2016 titled ‘Germany’. As we’ve come to expect from him, the single retains the solid grooves, percussion, and layering that one gets from his productions. A funky bass line is the backbone of the track that moves between two notes, a driving rhythm keeps the energy up, and effected samples ebb and flow creating a festive sounding piece. The appropriately titled ‘Eric’s S-Bahn Mix’ takes Tony’s ideas and morphs them, creating a crossover track that blurs the lines between, house, techno, and tech-house. Echoing voices with a fat bottom end, house chords, and hints of acid take the original and launch it into complete peak time territory. It compliments the original version splendidly.
Get your huge speakers out for this one – this single is guaranteed to light a dance floor on fire.

title: The Capability EP
review: Sleepy & Boo are certainly no strangers to the New York City electronic music circuit, and we’re proud to have ‘The Capability EP’ for their debut on 3Bridge Records. This three-track release of solid techno is fully capable of getting a dance floor moving, all night long.

‘Alignment’ gets things started right out of the gate, with solid shuffling percussion and a rumbling bass line laying the groove foundation. Synth pads and whispering vocals swell in and out, creating a cavernous warehouse sound, along with subtle melodic flourishes that give it soul. ‘Acceptance’ has a similar feel, only this time the music goes a bit darker, with chaotic arpeggiation underneath the groove, and thick square bass hits that drive it. You need a techno jam for a 5am set? Look no further. ‘Articulate’ is the most house influenced tune on the EP, with its kick and layered cymbals as the main percussive elements, coupled with jacking chicago-house type stabs that keep the rhythms going until the very end.

title: Gone Away EP
review: 3Bridge Records proudly presents the first release of 2016 from producer Eric Shans, the ”Gone Away EP”. It showcases his penchant for rich infectious hooks and sounds, as well as affection for emotive music.

Title track ‘Gone Away’ is replete with heavy symphonic elements, guitar, and synth-pop type vocals carried over catchy bass lines and finely layered percussion. Melancholic lyrics complete the tune, but a sense of hope also permeates. ‘Who Will Save Us’ takes a similar approach but with a even more mountainous soundtrack feel with expansive harmonized vocals and pads giving it lots of depth and dimension. And ‘Red Stars Burst’ closes out the EP with beautiful strings, sparkling atmospherics, and gentle passages to wind everything down.
Uplifting and hopeful, and at the same time mournful and reflective, this EP lets us know that life is full of moments where we need to remind ourselves that we’re human.

title: Chaotic
review: To kick off 2016, we present Deep Woods’ latest release ‘Chaotic’. As winter descends upon us, this track will comfort you with its warm blankets of choirs, spoken word samples, melodic washes of synths, and smooth percussion. Mysterious and mythical, it’s a superb piece of work that’d fit into a DJ’s set at any point of the night or day, as well as being an imaginary soundtrack to a fantasy film. Eric Shans’ version takes the celestial, atmospheric nature of the original and drives it a bit harder, layering the elements on top of a huge bass line and crunchy drums to give it a huge peak hour feel. It’ll get people moving and shaking while looking for the sunlight poking through the glass in the early sunrise of the morning or those flickers of illuminating LEDs in a dark warehouse or club. This release should be in any music connoisseur’s collection.

tracks.title: Chaotic (Eric's Headed For The Sun Mix)

title: The Best Of 3Bridge Volume 1
review: We at 3Bridge are proud of all of the releases on the label from the the past few years. Just in time for the holidays, we wanted to highlight some of our favorite tracks. This wasn’t easy, as there are a lot of them that we love, but we tried to cover a huge span of both sounds and styles that represent what the label is about – putting good music first above and beyond anything else. Here’s to hoping you enjoy the first collection of our hand picked gems! Be on the lookout for a second volume in 2016.

title: Memories EP
review: Minimal techno artist LGR (aka Luis Miguel Ascencio ) is back with another release on the label, the ‘Memories EP’. This 3 track has a lot of character with exquisite sound design and superb production.

‘Isabeel’ ebbs and flows with interesting sampling, echoed voices, and subtle evolving atmospheres, all backed by a techno focused dance floor beat. ‘Memories’ takes that approach as well, and adds thick bass lines that filter in and out along with melodies that swim beneath the surface. And closing track ‘Regresar Al Pasado’ which translates to ‘Going Back To The Past’, brings it all home, combining sharp analog sounding leads, minimal percussion, and great sampling work.
We’re excited for LGR and his second release on our label.

title: Happy Warrior (Nadja Lind Remix)
review: Originally released in April of 2015, the track ‘Happy Warrior’ was the second original track that Eric Shans and Jay Hill released on 3Bridge Records. It now gets a rework from Berlin, Germany’s Nadja Lind, who is a veteran producer and DJ, owner of the Lucidflow label imprint, and one half of the duo Klartraum. Nadja’s remix takes the driving and atmospheric elements of the original and contains them within a hefty set of dark techno beats, shuffling bass lines, and patterned synth workouts. It’s meant to played on monumentally sized speakers in a dimly lit nightclub (or warehouse), or a festival to ten thousand gyrating bodies. There’s also an underlying sense of groovy fun to it as well which gives it even more playability. To say we’re excited to have this in the 3Bridge Records arsenal is an understatement. Take the remixed journey of the ‘Happy Warrior’.

title: I’ll Be So Good (The Remixes)
artistLine: Deep Woods, Eric Shans, Roberto Pedoto
review: Roberto Pedoto had originally released “I’ll Be So Good” on the Aqua-Booty! Imprint and now it’s getting a re-release on 3Bridge Records. It has quickly become a go-to record to get a crowd moving. This is truly an addictive house track with a memorable bass line, a unique vocal, and sunny groove.

Deep Woods has captured a number of original elements in his remix while putting his signature sounds and special groove to it. Eric Shans tries another approach with keeping it true to its main idea but injecting his distinct sound throughout resulting in a dirty, fun approach.

We hold this one dear to our hearts as DJs and the label, and we’re proud to give it another release. The crowds will come alive as soon as it hits their ears and any version on this single will be sure to tear up a dance floor. Be good to yourself and pick it up.

tracks.title: I'll Be So Good (Deep Woods Remix)
I'll Be So Good (Eric Shans Remix)

title: Yours And Mine EP
review: Eric Shans’ latest EP comes right in time for your summer days and nights. Never afraid to push the infinite possibilities of electronic music, both tracks here stand out on their own, with funky, groovy sounds that provide a canopy of warmth and melody.

The title track’s main elements slowly build over time as the piece moves along. A soulful vocal repeats, pads and strings crescendo in and out, all while cascading over sultry beats and bass lines that strike through the listener’s heart. This is sure to capture people’s ears that appreciate the softer, dreamier side of house music.

“Behind Feelings” also takes a similar stance, toughening up on the drums just a little, all while maintaining an ethereal, yet danceable atmosphere. Fat bottom end, shimmering synths, and a catchy vocal will make the beach sun even brighter, that poolside cocktail taste even better, or it might even capture a memorable moment inside of a dark club.
We at 3Bridge pride ourselves at releasing good, innovative music. This EP is no exception.

title: Hunt Or Be Hunted
review: 3Bridge head honcho Deep Woods is back with a sweltering, groovy, atmospheric single that truly encompasses his sound. Always willing to push and blur the lines between genres, he’s created a track that exercises this approach, with brooding synth lines, layered shuffled percussion, and a stomping rhythm. Late or early night, it’ll work great in a big or small room.

Eric’s remix takes Deep Woods’ vision and takes it in an even more sinister direction, while still maintaining a groove that’s designed for peak time sets. Putting his own trademark bass line-synth driven spin on things, it’s a banger of a track that will get heads nodding and bodies shaking with hands in the air.
As the sample’s message dictates…hunt before you are yourself the one hunted.

tracks.title: Hunt Or Be Hunted (Eric's Run For Your Life Remix)

title: In The Line – EP
review: A new signing for 3Bridge, we proudly present LGR’s (aka Luis Miguel Ascencio) “In The Line EP”. These 2 tracks demonstrate his ability to precisely craft and create atmospheric minimal techno that would fit right into a DJ’s set at any point in the night or day.

The title track “In The Line” takes silky smooth pads and vocals while interweaving them with slick beats alongside exquisite sound design that flows throughout. The result is a subtle funky number, meant to be played loudly over a booming sound system where its scale can truly be shown.

“MTA Power” is a bit of a play on words as its locomotive rhythms and patterns echo that of a certain transit system local to the New York area. Strange noises filter in and out, steady drums and hi-hats propel it, all while abstract melodies dip in between all of this – very similar to taking a long subway ride, late at night.
Truly interesting stuff if we do say so ourselves. Get in between the lines with this EP.

title: Separated Distance EP
review: Just in time for summer, the “Separated Distance” EP is the newest release from Eric Shans on 3Bridge. This EP showcases his penchant for dreamy, lush sounds and it contains 2 mixes of the track “Separated By A Certain Distance” and the song “Path Home”, an ambient opus which would fit well in any expansive, epic film.

Bright, celestial sounding chords, beautiful strings, and overall subtle yet effective touches highlight both the vocal and dub mix, the former contains an additional layer; harmonized effected vocals that could have been sung from the heavens. It also has a steady dance groove and would fit well into a daytime party as the sun descends, or an early morning beachfront set while waves cascade over white sands. “Path Home” rounds off this EP well as it gives the listener a journey that builds over time with heavy swirling pads, radio static effects, and light percussive elements.This EP is a shining beacon meant for any season where you need some warmth and emotion in your music.

tracks.title: Separated By A Certain Distance (Vocal Mix)
Separated By A Certain Distance (Dub Mix)

title: The Classic Instinct
review: Once again, the producers who go by the moniker Brocartel keep reminding us that the Ukraine is alive and well with creativity in the electronic arena, and it’s shown by their latest offering on 3Bridge Records, called “The Classic Instinct”. Alive with haunting pianos and whispered female vocals, the track is layered with powerful beats, deadly bass lines, and top notch riffs. It’s a peak hour jam sure to tear through any dance floor and even get those bystanders moving by getting them drawn into the groove.

With remix support from the prolific Deep Woods, his version takes a darker dive with hints of the track’s elements swimming in the distance. Maintaining a soul shaking groove throughout, it provides a great compliment to the original.
This is the Brocartel’s 3rd release on 3Bridge and they have shown that they do not disappoint.

title: Star Bird
review: Spanish producer Tony Crawm is back with his first release on 3Bridge for 2015. Almost an extension of his first single “The Isotopes”, “Star Bird” is a techno destroyer of a tune that grooves with a tough approach and at the same time having melodic undertones that permeate throughout. Strong sub bass lines set the tone and smooth driving beats, echoed mechanical rhythms, and fluttered starry patterns make sure that you’ll be moving on a dance floor near you. Peak time solid techno from a producer you’ll hear lots more of in the months to come.

title: Thoughts Like Waves EP
review: Prolific producer Eric Shans is back with another release on 3Bridge that’s already getting worldwide support. This 2 track is destined to make a mark. Title track “Thoughts Like Waves” struck the ears of DJs already before it’s release and now it’s officially ready and guaranteed to get a floor moving. Striking house chords and sequences, along with tight-knit arrangements, fat bottom end, and syncopated danceable rhythms with vocals make this a gem and regardless of a DJs personal style, it will fit nicely in their collection. “Return From The Dark” explores the realms of outer space sounding techno but really, it would work in a club here on Earth just as well. It’s a journey that takes the listener from the deep depths of the planet upwards towards the gradual illuminating light that shines through the clouds. Distant chopped up voices, booming bass and percussion, and smacking grooves that hold it all together, it’s a perfect compliment to the A-side.

title: Just About To Lose My Mind
review: Deep Woods strikes again with his second release of 2015 on 3Bridge. This single truly is evocative of the New York City house scene of the 80s and 90s taking the soulful vocal cues from that era while incorporating smooth pads, nostalgic synth lines and a jumping bass line that will get people’s bodies movin’ and shakin’. This track is made for anyone who wants some pure soul in their house music.

Italian producer Roberto Pedotos remix steps back the energy a bit to give the track a bit more space while retaining the truly classic house sound of the original. Pedoto incorporates the catchy vocal line while filling the track with crisp hi hats and drums, funky bass riffs, and buttery organ chords. Groovy and sunny, it’s perfect for the upcoming warmer months.

tracks.title: Just About To Lose My Mind (Original Mix)
Just About To Lose My Mind ( Roberto Pedoto Remix)

title: Happy Warrior
review: “Happy Warrior” is the second collaboration project of Jay Hill and Eric Shans. As of late, the duo has begun to develop a strong reputation for championing their own unique blend of deep house-not-deep-house, techno-not-techno music. This piece is a rare culmination that evolved over several months – starting with the duo passing back and forth a series of sounds and musical riffs along with experimenting with things like middle eastern percussion hits and vocals. It all evolved and ended up as a sophisticated sonic exploration that only artists like Jay and Eric could execute beautifully in union. Muti-dimensional, original, and at the same time danceable, “Happy Warrior” is a truly symbiotic exercise in two minds coming together to create something magical.

The result is mystical, spacey clutch of deep house and techno crossover – blessed with delightfully loose drums, undulating chords, middle eastern percussions, intriguing vocal bits, and contagious rhythms that graciously invite multiple listens without being too insinuating. While there are actual lyrics to the track, it is clear the vocalizations are used primarily as expressive, warm layers of sound. The finished product is hard to resist, avoiding the trap of being too shallow and catchy, and has a lasting allure. Eric and Jay are on the frontier of new and exciting musical creations

title: Mirror
review: 3Bridge Records is proud to present the 2nd release of 2015 from Eric Shans, the single “Mirror”. In contrast to some of the material on his previous EP this year on 3Bridge, this track takes a tougher tech house approach guaranteed to get people moving. Replete with rugged bass lines, effected vocals, and punchy percussion, it’s meant for later in the night when people are ready to groove. Within the rawness though, there’s a sense of playful warmth and melody that grab and hook the listener in.

Pete Schwinge, who has remixed a number of tracks for Eric on 3Bridge, takes an epic, night time, widescreen approach to the track. In this mix, his talented penchant for creating layers and walls of sound, on top of driving percussive beats is showcased as he transforms the song into a behemoth of sound design and production. It’s the soundtrack to a figurative hall of twisted mirrors where your mind and body will roam.

title: The Dreamer
review: One of the best producers of our time, Rick Wade brings us 2 new tracks to 3Bridge Records. A bit different than his usual works, he uses his diverse production skills to bring us 2 gems.

“The Dreamer” takes layered pads and glides them over hypnotic percussion and they’re attached to a flowing, sub-bass line that propels the atmosphere. It gives the feeling of flying steadily through the skies, looking at the world beneath.

“Sky Barrier” gives us a similar feeling, but with a slightly stripped down approach. Rumbling bass, fuzzy strings, and slick percussion are the main elements here, and this formula turns it into a solid piece of dance music.

title: World Fell Down
review: Eric Shans starts the new year off with a 3 song EP that showcases his diverse styles as a producer. Always trying to push the envelope, his productions are rarely predictable, however they all have a sound that pays homage to many different electronic genres. We present to you the “World Fell Down” EP. The title track is a shining example of his deeper musical visions- slow and steady house beats, beautiful melodies, symphonic strings, and a warm bass surround the listener while ethereal vocals get delivered from the heavens. The result is a completely playable, yet original composition where the emotion shines through. “Patterns” goes for a bit of a different sound, and it’s higher energy and more immediate. The result is a fun tech house romp, with bouncing analog bass lines, old school house hits, science fiction type samples, and high throttled percussion that will fill any dance floor. “All End Now” is the most electronic pop driven song on the EP, and it’s got influences of 80s new wave dance music with shimmering pads, thick low end, and yearning vocals with catchy melodies. Lyrically on the darker side, but musically bright and hopeful, it’s the perfect paradox of a track that will win everyone over.

title: Take Me Higher
review: Deep Woods kicks off the new year with his latest release, “Take Me Higher”. Taking cues from 90s house music and the current deep sounds of today, he’s produced a dance floor workout which is guaranteed to get people’s heads bobbing and feet moving. Both retro and futuristic while being funky, bumping, and soulful, this one goes back to roots of the Deep Woods sound. Detroit staple Rick Wade’s remix takes the track even further into classic house territory and produces something that would fit in any deep house DJ’s crate. It especially harkens back to the days of legendary parties in New York, like Shelter and 718 Sessions where a track dropped like this would have people dancing and singing like there was no tomorrow. Soft emotive pads cascade over a repeated vocal phrase, which is all driven by Roland style percussion and a chunky bass line. The result is a tremendous rework.

title: The Isotopes
review: Spanish producer Tony Crawm (aka Antonio Laguna) delivers 2 slices of funky, groovy workouts on his latest release “The Isotopes”. Tony is a new signing for 3Bridge and this single is an indication that his future is bright. The title track “The Isotopes” is chock full of deeply layered percussion, full low tones, and sweeping atmospheres all sprinkled with vocal samples, warped effects, and hypnotic loops. “Don’t Judge” also takes this formula and adds a bit more throttle to the energy, and is meant for deep in the night (or morning). Stuttering vocals, tightly sequenced rhythms, and a killer bass line shift this into high gear and it’ll light up any dance floor it’s played on. Tony Crawm is an artist to watch, and we are proud to present his first release.

title: Dreamcatcher (Giuliano Rodrigues Remix)
review: Brazilian producer Giuliano Rodrigues drops a bomb on the world with his remix of “Dreamcatcher”, the track by Eric Shans released a few months back. Utilizing his skilled production techniques, he has morphed it into a monstrous dance floor workout designed for any peak time set. Composed of towering percussion, rattling low end, locomotive type rhythms, and treated vocal phrases that melodically swim deep in the mix, he has created a stunning rework that will be sure to light any room on fire. Giuliano has a style that is all his own and it makes him a force to reckoned with in the electronic music world.

title: Our Hands
review: Producer Eric Shans strikes again with the single “Our Hands”. Always trying to push the envelope with dance music, he brings in an amalgam of styles meant for any dance floor. Weaving dreamy pads and strings, tight driving percussion, tough bass lines, and yearning vocals; this track is one that you’ll gladly wrap yourself in.

Giuliano Rodrigues’ mix breaks apart some of these main elements, and instead creates a motion ridden and expansive collage of sounds with deeply layered drums, subtle low end, and alien soundscapes. Eric’s vox are meticulously placed in the space between in this aural world and this formula makes for a fantastic rendition of the track.

title: Last Night I Went Deep
review: Deep Woods brings us a bit of a different feel with this more light hearted track full of bounce and fun. Inspired by his roots in the 90’s house scene, “Last Night I Went Deep” brings the fun into the deep driving beats and bass line that truly makes this a dance floor winner. The dub version includes Deep Woods style murky dark feel, his signature sound for all your underground needs.
