title: Skylights (The Remixes)
artistLine: Eric Shans, Giuliano Rodrigues, Jay Hill
review: 2014 has been quite the year for releases on 3Bridge Records. We’re excited to present the track “Skylights”, reinterpreted in fantastic form by both Tolis Q (Quantized Music) and Giuliano Rodrigues (Flowing Movement Music). Both producers offer vastly different takes, and they add diversity and playability to this single. Tolis has put together a stellar remix that takes Jay’s skyward facing vocals and makes them a central focal point, while filling the track with driving bass lines, shimmering pads, tightly programmed percussion, and smartly layered synth sounds that strike through the heart. This is meant for any DJ’s crate as it spans the house sub-genre spectrum and is perfect for a room both big and small.

Giuliano’s version uses Eric’s hypnotic vocals from the original and towers them over the track’s sonic landscape, while Jay’s echo underneath, giving everything a dark, amazingly spacious, widescreen feel. Layered minimalistic pumping techno beats and interplanetary sounds ebb and flow throughout, rumbling through the speakers. Whether it’s at an after party, in a warehouse at peak time, or an opening at an art gallery, it’s sure to go over splendidly.

title: We Go On
review: Rick Wade is back on 3Bridge Records and what a delight it is to have him with a new single and it’s the first in a series of 2 he’ll be putting out for the label in 2016. ‘We Go On’ is true slice of soulful deep house filled with everything you love about the genre: eloquent vocals, smooth chords, smoky sax riffs, and funky, danceable beats. This is the kind of piece that would work at any time of the day or night. Label head honcho Deep Woods takes this track into mildly techier territory, while keeping all of the soul intact. Steady percussive rhythms and main organ stabs guide the track through its course, while the vocals of the original flow in and out doing the original more than justice. Mr. Wade has delivered for 3Bridge once again!

title: Symbiotic EP
review: Futureworlder (aka Brian Traister) returns with his second release on the label of 2017. Like his previous release, it’s 4 pieces of moving, deep melodic tech workouts that would be great for any DJ’s set.

‘Light Me Up’ starts things off properly with huge cathedral type leads that coast over tough techno drums and racing 16th notes. You could picture a thousand bodies gyrating in sync to this on a beach island or in an off the beaten path warehouse in an unknown location. ‘Introspective’ pulls back the energy a bit but it’s no less captivating. Big thick analog pads float over a rubbery bass line, and later on, old school acid riffs give it an extra dose of grit. ‘Symbiotic’ comes back to the big dance floor formula and has a fantastic sense of motion to it. Sweet, fluttering, robust chords run in and out of the mix as energetic hats, a fat kick, and percussion propel it forward. And the closer, ‘What Your Heart Tells You,’ has a beautiful progression of melody that really give it soul and resolve while having a bit of filth in the bass line; a nice paradox to bring the EP to a close.
We’re super stoked about this second release on 3Bridge from Futureworlder.

title: Sexting With Strangers
review: Label head Eric Shans returns to 3Bridge Records with X Miss Ella on their new EP ‘Sexting With Strangers’. It’s a fun return to the warmer months ahead with 2 original tunes that bring home their trademark vocal driven dirty house sound. They’ve created an EP that will light up the party.

The ‘Sex And Dinner’ original mix takes big drums, bottom heavy bass lines, filthy synth riffs, and Ella’s sultry vox that tell a fun, debauched story. The ‘Acid Mix’ goes more into heavier tech house house territory with crazy effects, layered percussion, and pristine grooves. ‘Sparkly Unicorn’ closes things out and its acidic bass, sharp thumps, and Ella’s lyrics that highlight the playful yet groovy tone of the piece really make this a stellar track. We all are in need of a little escapism and this set of music will provide it.
Mastered by Jeff Clarke.

title: Ping Pong
review: We welcome Simon Sampler back to the label for a great 2 tracker featuring Austrian producer Fischmehl as well. “Wetterwand” is a pitched down deep house affair with floating pads, big bass lines, and echoed vocals. “Ping Pong” amps up the energy with its hypnotic techno delivery. Off kilter melodies, racing hi hats, and synthesized hits is the formula here.

title: Martians
review: A veteran DJ and producer, Mark Ryal is yet another new addition to the 3Bridge roster. He brings to us 4 new tracks on his EP ‘Martians’. It’s an original and unique take on deep house and it is simply fantastic.

‘Virgo’ starts things off with a smooth bass line, smooth flowing pads, big kicks, and whip like snares. It’s a great way to kick off the EP. You’ll hear shadows of Chicago influenced house in here too, upping the deepness. ‘Red To The Horizon’ has some almost jazzy influences. Live sounding synth riffs play over a sub bass, and pianos and liquid synth sounds cascade through the mix. Mark keeps it interesting, there’s no predictable patterns here, just straight ahead funkiness and evolving grooves. ‘Surface’ takes effected layers of sound and melody and places them on an aural ping pong set as laid back percussive elements drive the rhythms. Lastly, ‘The Iberian Martian’ brings things down a bit, fittingly. Big expansive melodies play over the piece; it’s almost as if it’s the soundtrack to go back to your own planet after being in a foreign world in your mind or otherwise.
Mr. Ryal has created something truly original in the world of house music. Pick this EP up, you sure won’t be disappointed you did.

title: Hemp EP
artistLine: Eric Shans, KP Deep Mesh, Second City Firsts
review: We welcome South African producer KP Deep Mesh (aka Khumbulani Nhlapo) to the 3Bridge Records family with his newest EP called ‘Hemp’. It features remixes by another newcomer to 3Bridge, Second City Firsts (aka Steve ‘Griffo’ Griffiths) as well as Eric Shans, one of the label bosses.

KP’s original mix features the best elements of classic deep house along with modern style analog riffs giving the piece a great groove. Crispy stabs resonate over shuffling, grainy hats with precision and subtle melodic touches grace the piece. The ‘Second City Firsts Heaven Scent Mix’ highlights these elements but switches the drums around a bit softening the clap and hats, and adding quite a cheeky sample. Both compliment each other well and come just in time for summer terrace parties.

‘Taken Away’ is moodier in its delivery but no less captivating; it’s a great warm up track that’s soulful and enriching. KP’s trademark buzzing stab sounds permeate throughout with saxophone riffs and bongos as well. Minor keys soundtrack a dark cityscape, lit up by fog and twinkling lights. And finally the ‘Eric Shans Fly High Remix’ injects a bit more techiness into the proceedings along with his trademark punchy drums and bright pads giving it some skyward facing moments. It ups the energy just a tad from the original.
We’re excited for KPs Deep Mesh’s first release on the label.

title: A Farewell To Kings
review: 3Bridge Records welcomes another new signing, the duo of Gianni Ruocco and Le Roi Carmona. We’re honored to be putting out a great new single by them with a remix by label head, Eric Shans.

The original mix demonstrates some serious production techniques and grooves. Echoed synth riffs and sequences play off the precise percussion that shuffles and shakes. Interestingly, there’s beauty underneath the grit and darkness; visions of subtle sunny melodies jabbing holes in the top of a dilapidated chapel to let the sunlight, while bodies dance and sway beneath it. At the heart of it though, there lies a great tech house track guaranteed to get people moving.

The ‘Eric Shans Royal Crown Remix’ takes a more straightforward approach but it’s no less captivating. Building a track around one of the main melodies of the original, Shans flips it into a dreamy, steady builder. It’s almost as if the remix is up in the clouds, while the original sits below it as they gaze at each other from afar. Two bass lines play off of each other while choirs, pads, and other elements create a razor sharp amalgam of patterns.
Say your ‘farewell to kings’ and pick up this release.
